name: Turkey
governanceModel: Sectoral guidance and a stalled draft AI law, paired with a new state-led compute and data-infrastructure push
debateTopics: AI-powered surveillance expansion outpacing Turkey's stalled comprehensive AI law
Turkey's Grok content ban as a precedent for state control over foreign AI chatbots
overview:
Turkey has no single, binding AI-specific statute in force as of mid-2026. A comprehensive draft Artificial Intelligence Law (Bill No. 2/2234), submitted to the Grand National Assembly in June 2024 and modeled loosely on the EU AI Act's risk-based structure, has reportedly stalled in committee, with legal commentators suggesting it is unlikely to pass in its current form given the limited parliamentary weight of the party that introduced it. In its place, governance has proceeded through sectoral guidance: the Personal Data Protection Authority (KVKK), which administers Law No. 6698, published a 'Guidelines on Generative AI and the Protection of Personal Data (in 15 Questions)' in November 2025 and followed with guidance on agentic AI systems in March 2026. Separately, a narrower draft law on AI-generated content — introducing mandatory 'Generated by Artificial Intelligence' labeling for deepfakes and penal-code amendments — was submitted to parliament in November 2025.

Alongside this thin regulatory layer, the government has pursued a large infrastructure- and industry-focused strategy. In June 2026, President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan unveiled 'Türkiye's Artificial Intelligence Vision and Action Plan (2026-2030),' targeting at least $10 billion in largely private-sector investment, a national data-center capacity of at least 1 gigawatt by 2030, and workforce programs aiming to train 10,000 advanced AI specialists and 100,000 application professionals. The plan sits within a broader push that includes a defense sector already active in AI-enabled systems (via Baykar, ASELSAN and HAVELSAN) and a domestic model ecosystem (T3 AI, TÜBİTAK's Bilge, HAVELSAN's MAIN platform) still relatively untested against international benchmarks. Meanwhile, rights groups and independent journalists have documented a rapid, largely unregulated expansion of AI-enabled facial-recognition surveillance used against protesters, and in July 2025 Turkey became the first country to open a legal probe into and block content from Elon Musk's Grok chatbot over statements about Erdoğan, Atatürk and religious values — developments that sit uneasily alongside the country's still-unresolved comprehensive AI law.

policyDirection.label: Large infrastructure push, stalled comprehensive AI law

atAGlance.regulatoryApproach: Sectoral guidance from the data protection authority (KVKK) layered on a draft comprehensive AI law that has stalled in parliamentary committee since mid-2024
atAGlance.latestMajorUpdate: Government unveiled Türkiye's Artificial Intelligence Vision and Action Plan (2026-2030), targeting at least $10B in mostly private investment (June 2026)
atAGlance.governmentInvolvement: High and growing — led by the Presidency's Digital Transformation Office and the Ministry of Industry and Technology, with state-linked defense firms central to domestic model development
atAGlance.industrialStrategy: 2026-2030 Action Plan targets roughly 1GW of data-center capacity, a National Data Library of 2,000+ public datasets, and training for 10,000 advanced AI specialists plus 100,000 application professionals
atAGlance.internationalPartnerships: Turkcell's hyperscale cloud partnership with Google Cloud (Ankara; Türkiye set to become Google Cloud's 43rd region) and AWS's new Istanbul Local Zone, alongside a proposed joint large language model for Turkic languages via the Organization of Turkic States
atAGlance.primaryPolicyFocus: Scaling compute and data infrastructure under the new Action Plan, while a comprehensive draft AI law remains stalled and narrower rules (generative-AI guidance, deepfake labeling) advance piecemeal

currentDirection.summary: Turkey's direction is mixed but leans toward tighter state involvement: a large state-backed compute and industrial buildout is proceeding rapidly under the 2026-2030 Action Plan, while on the rules side KVKK has issued successive binding-adjacent guidance on generative and agentic AI, a deepfake-labeling bill is moving through parliament, and authorities have shown a willingness to block AI chatbot content outright (the Grok case). The one comprehensive, EU-AI-Act-style framework that would set clear risk-based obligations — the 2024 draft AI law — remains stalled, so in practice Turkey's AI governance is advancing through narrower, faster-moving instruments rather than a single overarching statute.

recentDevelopments.text: President Erdoğan unveils 'Türkiye's Artificial Intelligence Vision and Action Plan (2026-2030)' at the Türkiye Artificial Intelligence Summit, committing at least $10B (mostly private investment) toward data centers, compute and workforce programs.

KVKK (Personal Data Protection Authority) issues guidance addressing agentic AI systems, joining a small group of data protection authorities (including the UK's ICO, Spain's AEPD and the EU's EDPS) to publish such guidance.
Turkcell and Google Cloud agree to build Türkiye's first hyperscale regional data center in Ankara, with Türkiye set to become Google Cloud's 43rd global region under a joint roughly $3B investment.

KVKK publishes 'Guidelines on Generative AI and the Protection of Personal Data (in 15 Questions),' its first comprehensive interpretation of how Turkey's data protection law applies across the generative-AI lifecycle.

A draft law amending the Turkish Penal Code and related statutes to regulate AI-generated content — including mandatory deepfake labeling and content-blocking requirements — is submitted to the Grand National Assembly.

Turkey becomes the first country to open a formal legal probe into, and block content from, Elon Musk's Grok AI chatbot, after it generated posts deemed insulting to Erdoğan, Atatürk and religious values.

policyAndRegulation.title: Draft Artificial Intelligence Law (Bill No. 2/2234)
policyAndRegulation.summary: Comprehensive, EU AI Act-influenced draft submitted to parliament in June 2024, proposing risk-based obligations and a registry for high-risk systems (e.g., medical diagnostics, autonomous transport). Legal commentary as of March 2026 suggests it is stalled in committee and unlikely to pass in its current form.

policyAndRegulation.title: Draft Law on Measures Concerning AI-Generated Content
policyAndRegulation.summary: Submitted November 7, 2025; would require deepfakes to carry a 'Generated by Artificial Intelligence' label (with fines up to TRY 5 million for non-compliance), mandate blocking of harmful AI content within six hours, and impose dataset-transparency obligations on providers.

policyAndRegulation.title: Law No. 6698 on the Protection of Personal Data (KVKK)
policyAndRegulation.summary: Turkey's general data protection law, which KVKK has increasingly applied to AI systems via sector guidance rather than new binding legislation.

policyAndRegulation.title: KVKK Guidelines on Generative AI and Personal Data Protection (15 Questions)
policyAndRegulation.summary: Non-binding but influential November 2025 guidance applying KVKK principles across the generative-AI lifecycle, covering training data, deployment and use.

policyAndRegulation.title: KVKK Guidance on Agentic AI
policyAndRegulation.summary: March 2026 guidance addressing personal-data risks specific to autonomous, tool-using AI agents.

policyAndRegulation.title: Türkiye's Artificial Intelligence Vision and Action Plan (2026-2030)
policyAndRegulation.summary: Government-adopted national plan (not binding legislation) built around discovery, use, production and governance, with data-center capacity, workforce and public-investment targets.

researchEcosystem.summary: AI-relevant research runs through METU (Middle East Technical University, which has announced efforts to build a dedicated AI hub), Bilkent University, Boğaziçi University's Institute for Data Science and Artificial Intelligence, and Koç University, alongside TÜBİTAK's public-sector AI research including its 'Bilge' model. A meaningful share of applied AI R&D also sits inside state-linked defense firms (ASELSAN, HAVELSAN, Baykar) rather than purely academic settings, reflecting the government's stated ambition to replicate its defense-industry gains in civilian AI.

companies.name: Baykar
companies.description: Drone manufacturer central to Turkey's defense-AI push; developer of the AI-enabled KEMANKEŞ 1 miniature cruise missile and, with the T3 Foundation, of the T3 AI model that entered beta via the government-linked NSosyal social platform in July 2025.

companies.name: ASELSAN
companies.description: State-linked defense electronics company developing AI-enabled targeting, sensor and autonomous-systems technology.

companies.name: HAVELSAN
companies.description: Defense and enterprise software company operating the MAIN platform, reported to include a nine-billion-parameter domestic language model.

companies.name: Turkcell
companies.description: Turkey's largest telecom operator and data-center provider, partnering with Google Cloud to build Türkiye's first hyperscale AI data-center region in Ankara.

companies.name: Trendyol
companies.description: E-commerce decacorn applying large-scale recommendation and logistics AI across its marketplace.

companies.name: Insider
companies.description: Turkish-founded marketing-technology unicorn using AI for customer engagement and growth-marketing products, with a significant international customer base.

providers.name: Turkcell / Google Cloud
providers.description: Joint venture (announced November 2025) to build Türkiye's first hyperscale regional data center in Ankara, with Türkiye becoming Google Cloud's 43rd global region under a roughly $3B combined investment; construction targeted to begin in Q1 2026 with full capacity by 2028.

providers.name: AWS
providers.description: Operates an AWS Local Zone in Istanbul (general availability announced May 2026), providing local compute and storage without a full AWS region.

universities.name: Middle East Technical University (METU)
universities.description: Public research university that has announced plans to build a dedicated AI hub as part of Turkey's broader AI competitiveness push.

universities.name: Bilkent University
universities.description: Private research university with AI and machine learning coursework and research within its Computer Engineering department.

universities.name: Boğaziçi University
universities.description: Hosts the Institute for Data Science and Artificial Intelligence, offering doctoral training in data science and AI.

thinkTanks.name: SETA (Foundation for Political, Economic and Social Research)
thinkTanks.description: Ankara-based think tank that has published analysis on Turkey's national AI strategy and framed AI policy as an instrument of Turkish foreign-policy autonomy.

governmentInstitutions.name: Digital Transformation Office of the Presidency (CBDDO)
governmentInstitutions.description: Presidency body co-leading Turkey's national AI strategy work alongside the Ministry of Industry and Technology; headed by Ali Taha Koç.

governmentInstitutions.name: Ministry of Industry and Technology
governmentInstitutions.description: Co-leads national AI strategy and the 2026-2030 AI Action Plan; led by Minister Mehmet Fatih Kacır.

governmentInstitutions.name: Personal Data Protection Authority (KVKK)
governmentInstitutions.description: Independent authority administering Law No. 6698, which has issued the main body of Turkish AI-adjacent guidance to date (generative AI, agentic AI).

governmentInstitutions.name: TÜBİTAK
governmentInstitutions.description: The Scientific and Technological Research Council of Turkey, developer of the 'Bilge' domestic AI model and a funder of national AI R&D.

notableGaps.note: The 2024 draft AI Law (Bill 2/2234) remains stalled in committee as of 2026, so Turkey has no enacted, dedicated AI statute — governance instead runs through KVKK guidance and narrower sectoral bills.

No dedicated AI regulatory body exists yet; KVKK covers AI only insofar as it touches personal data, leaving non-data AI harms (e.g., safety of autonomous systems, algorithmic discrimination outside data protection) without a clear regulatory home.

Domestic models such as T3 AI, TÜBİTAK's Bilge and HAVELSAN's MAIN are described in government and industry sources, but none appear to have been independently benchmarked against leading international models; claims about their capabilities should be treated cautiously.

debates.topic: AI-powered surveillance expansion outpacing Turkey's stalled comprehensive AI law
debates.summary: Independent reporting has documented a rapid buildout of AI-enabled facial-recognition surveillance — including a March 2025 tender for 13,000 additional cameras and integration into the nationwide City Security Management System (KGYS) — deployed against protesters following the March 2025 arrest of Istanbul mayor Ekrem İmamoğlu, with no dedicated legal framework specifically governing this use.
debates.expanded: Interior Minister Ali Yerlikaya has publicly endorsed expanding facial-recognition-equipped body cameras and camera networks, and investigative journalists and rights groups report that roughly 2,000 people were detained and 239 formally imprisoned in the protests that followed İmamoğlu's arrest, with facial recognition cited as a tool used to identify protesters. This expansion has proceeded even as Turkey's one comprehensive AI bill remains stalled in parliamentary committee, meaning there is little indication that binding, AI-specific rules will constrain this kind of use in the near term. Human rights organizations argue this reflects a broader pattern in which state security applications of AI move faster than the legislative process meant to govern AI generally, though the government has not, in available reporting, directly addressed this specific criticism.

debates.topic: Turkey's Grok content ban as a precedent for state control over foreign AI chatbots
debates.summary: Turkey's July 2025 move to open a criminal probe into, and block content from, xAI's Grok chatbot after it generated posts deemed insulting to Erdoğan, Atatürk and religious values is described by some observers as the first instance of a government formally censoring an AI chatbot's outputs.
debates.expanded: Authorities framed the action as protecting the dignity of state institutions and religious values, consistent with existing Turkish restrictions on insulting the presidency; critics, including anti-censorship activists cited in international reporting, argue the case sets a template that other governments — including ones without Turkey's specific legal provisions — could invoke to justify blocking AI-generated content they find objectionable, under broad definitions of hate speech or national security. Because this action was taken under existing content-restriction law rather than new AI-specific legislation, it also illustrates how much of Turkey's practical AI governance to date has occurred outside any dedicated AI statute.
